purpose: Track the machines the factory can reach - outposts that receive work, do it and report back - together with their roles, lifecycle state, and ratification evidence.
purpose_original: Track hive-capable factory and Zo computer nodes, their roles, deployment state, and ratification evidence.

vocabulary.outpost: A SEPARATE MACHINE that can receive work, do it, and report back. Operator's definition, 2026-09-11. Narrower than the old word 'node': a script is not an outpost, a repository is not an outpost, and a machine that can only be pushed to is only an outpost once something on it can answer.
vocabulary.why_not_node: 'Node' is overloaded to the point of being dangerous here. It means the Node.js runtime, it means the SovereignNode repository (a separate product, with its own unrelated 'hive'), and it means DOM/tree/graph vertices. Only the hive-machine sense becomes 'outpost'. A blind rename across the word destroys the other three senses silently.
vocabulary.field_note: The `nodes` array keeps its key. Renaming the key would break every reader by path - tools/factory/node-heartbeat.cjs and tools/factory/build-tracker.cjs in the Telechurch repo both index `doc.nodes`. The concept is renamed; the wire format is not.

lifecycle.why: The schema could say `active` and nothing else, so three completely different situations all read as one. They are separated here because only one of them is a problem.

states.retired: Deliberately stood down. A decision was taken. Nothing is wrong.
states.stopped: It ran and then quit. Nobody decided that, and nobody noticed at the time.
states.never_started: Nothing ever fed it on its own. It only ever answered when pushed to, or it never ran at all. This is NOT the same as stopped, and calling it stopped invents a working period that never existed.

lifecycle.reader_warning: No reader enforces these. scripts/hive/hive-node-deployment-pack.mjs gates only on status !== 'blocked', so a retired outpost still reports ready_to_stage: true. See finding `retired-status-does-not-block-the-deployment-pack`.

All ten of its prior evidence entries span a single day, 2026-04-30T03:21Z to 12:15Z, and every one of them is the same shape: the Windows desktop pushed a bundle and got a syntax check back ('synced to ApostleJ; remote syntax check returncode=0'). So it functioned as a sync target and never as a self-running machine. Stated as observed, not inferred from silence: the absence of autonomous evidence is corroborated by the presence of that evidence on alliance, which proves the record WOULD have captured it.

nodes.name: Home Desk
nodes.role: The operator's own Windows desktop - the machine the Living Factory actually runs on. It is the first and currently the only outpost.
nodes.refounded_why: THIS ROW WAS NEVER A ZO COMPUTER, whatever it said. The thing writing its heartbeat is tools/factory/node-heartbeat.cjs in the Telechurch repo, running on the operator's Windows desktop with NODE_ID hardcoded to 'telechurch', and the extra data it reports is that PC's boot time and reboot-pending state. Its beat proves the desktop is running. Nothing in that path asks any Zo computer anything, and no Zo credential is involved. So retiring the Zo computers must not retire this row - it is the machine everything else runs on, and it is the honest first entry in an outpost register.
nodes.id_is_load_bearing: The id stays 'telechurch' even though the name changed. tools/factory/node-heartbeat.cjs matches on n.id === 'telechurch' and tools/factory/build-tracker.cjs finds this row the same way to render the board's host panel. Renaming the id would silently blank the board's host display and stop the heartbeat writing. Rename the label, never the key.
